faqs.q: What is the Parker 4MA tie rod air cylinder with intermediate male rod end, Rod Number 1, 1 1/2" bore?
faqs.a: It is a double-acting, non-lube NFPA tie-rod air cylinder from the Parker 4MA Series with a 1 1/2" bore, an intermediate male rod end and Parker rod code No. 1. This listing holds 104 built part numbers in the 1P4MA001 range, used for light pushing, stopping, gating and clamping on conveyors, assembly and packaging machines.

faqs.q: How do I read a 1P4MA001 part number such as 1P4MA0018828 in the Parker 4MA 1 1/2" bore range?
faqs.a: Each 1P4MA001 number identifies one complete 1 1/2" bore 4MA cylinder with its stroke, mounting and rod end already fixed, so it is ordered as a single code. For example, 1P4MA0018828 is a 1" stroke cylinder with sleeve nut (MX5). Every part number on this listing starts 1P4MA001; the size table gives stroke and mount for each one.

faqs.q: What stroke lengths does the Parker 4MA 1 1/2" bore Rod Number 1 cylinder come in?
faqs.a: The 104 part numbers in this 1 1/2" bore listing cover strokes from 0.5" to 40", with 1", 2", 4" and 6" the most common. Stroke is fixed in each part number, so pick the row that matches the travel you need; if no row matches, send the Parker model code or the bore, stroke and mount and we will quote the nearest build.

faqs.q: Which NFPA mounting styles are offered on the Parker 4MA 1 1/2" bore Rod Number 1 cylinder?
faqs.a: The most common mountings in this 1 1/2" bore listing are head rectangular flange (MF1), side tap (MS4), cap fixed clevis (MP1), cap detachable clevis (MP2) and side lug (MS2). Every row in the size table names its NFPA mounting code, so filter by the mount your machine already uses before choosing a stroke.

faqs.q: What operating temperature and pressure apply to the Parker 4MA 1 1/2" bore Rod Number 1 cylinder?
faqs.a: Parker specifies an ambient operating temperature of -10°F to +165°F (about -23°C to +74°C) for this 1 1/2" bore 4MA listing. The rows here do not carry a pressure figure; the companion 4MA Rod Number 2 and 3 listings are rated 250 psi, about 17 bar, and we confirm the rating of your part number with the quotation.

faqs.q: What is the Parker 4MA 1 1/2" bore Rod Number 1 cylinder made of?
faqs.a: The 1 1/2" bore 4MA has a hard-anodized aluminium cylinder body, an aluminium piston with a composite piston bearing, a bronze gland and rod bearing, and a hard chrome-plated carbon steel piston rod. It is a non-lube design for compressed air, so it runs on filtered, dry air without an oiler; fit a filter-regulator upstream to protect the seals.

faqs.q: Is the Parker 4MA 1 1/2" bore Rod Number 1 cylinder interchangeable with other NFPA cylinders?
faqs.a: Yes, the 4MA is built to NFPA tie-rod mounting conventions, so a 1 1/2" bore 4MA with the same NFPA mount, stroke and rod end will fit where another NFPA cylinder of that envelope was used. This listing carries no certificates; if you need a certificate of conformity or test record, ask for it in the enquiry and we request it from Parker with the order.

faqs.q: What port size and rod end does the Parker 4MA 1 1/2" bore Rod Number 1 cylinder use?

Parker specifies a special UNF rod-end thread, so state the thread you need at order. Matching NPT push-in fittings, flow controls and silencers are on our [pneumatic fittings shelf](/c/pneumatic-fittings-silencers).

Parker lists this build as repairable, with a magnetic piston and bumper seals. Our [cylinder cushioning and mounting guide](/blog/pneumatic-cylinder-cushioning-and-mounting) covers alignment couplers and buckling.
